knowledge-base.name: lang-lua
knowledge-base.triggers: Lua, .lua, LuaJIT, luajit, Neovim, neovim, Love2D, love2d, busted, luacheck, stylua, luarocks, nvim, init.lua
knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for Lua. Loaded automatically when agents work on .lua files. Applies to Lua 5.4+, LuaJIT 2.1, Neovim plugins, Love2D, and embedded scripting environments.

core-principles.principle: Arrays, maps, objects, modules, and namespaces are all tables. Master table construction, iteration, and metatables.
Always declare variables local. Globals are a performance and correctness hazard; they pollute the global environment and resist JIT optimization.
Use pcall/xpcall for recoverable errors; error() for programmer mistakes. Never silently swallow failures.
Use metatables for genuine OOP needs, not as decoration on simple data tables.
Lua exists to be embedded. Keep the host/script boundary clean and narrow; validate all arguments from host bindings.

guardrail.rule: Always declare variables local. Undeclared globals silently corrupt state and are not JIT-compiled in LuaJIT.
guardrail.good: local count = 0 -- local to current scope

guardrail.rule: Never silently swallow errors. Always log or propagate the error value from pcall/xpcall.
guardrail.bad: local ok = pcall(risky_fn) -- error message discarded
guardrail.good: local ok, err = pcall(risky_fn) if not ok then log.error("risky_fn failed: %s", err) end

guardrail.rule: Arrays are 1-based. Use for i = 1, #arr for indexed iteration. Do not mix array indices and string keys in the same table.
Return nil, err_msg from functions that can fail. This is idiomatic Lua error signaling; callers must check the first return value.
guardrail.bad: function read_file(path) local f = io.open(path, "r") return f:read("*a") -- panics if f is nil end
guardrail.good: local function read_file(path) local f, err = io.open(path, "r") if not f then return nil, "cannot open: " .. err end local content = f:read("*a") f:close() return content end

guardrail.rule: Use ipairs for sequential table iteration and pairs for hash-map iteration. Do not use pairs on sequence tables in hot paths (not JIT-compiled in LuaJIT).
Use table.concat instead of .. concatenation inside loops. String concatenation in a loop creates O(n^2) garbage.
guardrail.bad: local s = "" for _, v in ipairs(parts) do s = s .. v end -- O(n^2) allocations

guardrail.rule: Localize frequently called standard library functions in hot code: local insert = table.insert. This avoids repeated global table lookup.
Avoid closures inside hot loops. Each closure allocation creates garbage and prevents JIT trace compilation in LuaJIT.

code-style.item: Use local for every variable and function unless it must be global
Naming: snake_case for variables/functions, PascalCase for class-like tables, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants
Indent with 2 spaces; one statement per line; avoid semicolons
Use [[ ... ]] long strings for multi-line text and SQL/HTML templates
Prefer #tbl over table.getn() for sequence length

tables.item: Arrays are 1-based; for i = 1, #arr not for i = 0, #arr - 1
Use ipairs for sequential iteration, pairs for hash-map iteration
Do not mix array indices and string keys in the same table (undefined # behavior)
Use table.insert / table.remove for array ops; avoid manual index gaps
Freeze config tables by setting a __newindex metamethod that errors on write

error-handling.item: Use pcall(fn, ...) to catch errors; xpcall(fn, handler, ...) for tracebacks
Return nil, err_msg from functions that can fail (idiomatic two-value return)
Reserve error("msg", level) for violated preconditions (programmer errors)
Never silently swallow errors; always log or propagate

performance.item: Localize hot functions: local insert = table.insert
Avoid closures inside hot loops (allocates every iteration)
Use table.concat instead of .. concatenation in loops
LuaJIT: avoid pairs() in hot paths (not JIT-compiled); prefer arrays with ipairs
LuaJIT: use FFI (ffi.new, ffi.cast) for C struct access instead of Lua tables

embedding.item: Keep the Lua-to-host API surface small (fewer than 20 registered functions)
Validate all arguments from Lua in C/host bindings
Set memory limits via lua_setallocf or lua_gc configuration
Use debug.sethook instruction-count hooks for untrusted scripts

pattern.name: Module Pattern
pattern.description: Return a table M from each file. Keep implementation details local. This is the idiomatic Lua module boundary.
pattern.example:
local M = {} local TIMEOUT_MS = 5000
local function validate(data) assert(type(data) == "table", "expected table, got " .. type(data)) assert(data.name, "missing required field: name") end
function M.process(data) validate(data) return { status = "ok", name = data.name } end
return M

pattern.name: OOP via Metatables
pattern.description: Use __index on a class table for method lookup. Inheritance sets __index to the parent class.

pattern.name: Error Handling with pcall
pattern.example:
local function read_config(path) local f, err = io.open(path, "r") if not f then return nil, "cannot open config: " .. err end local content = f:read("*a") f:close() return content end
local ok, result = xpcall(dangerous_operation, debug.traceback) if not ok then log.error("failed: %s", result) end

pattern.name: Coroutines as Generators
pattern.example:
local function producer(items) return coroutine.wrap(function() for _, item in ipairs(items) do coroutine.yield(item) end end) end
local function filter(predicate, iter) return coroutine.wrap(function() for item in iter do if predicate(item) then coroutine.yield(item) end end end) end
local nums = producer({ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 }) local evens = filter(function(n) return n % 2 == 0 end, nums) for v in evens do print(v) end --> 2, 4, 6

pattern.name: Custom Iterator
pattern.example:
local function range(start, stop, step) step = step or 1 local i = start - step return function() i = i + step if i <= stop then return i end end end
for n in range(1, 10, 2) do print(n) end --> 1, 3, 5, 7, 9

pattern.name: Neovim Lua API
pattern.description: Use vim.tbl_deep_extend for option merging. Create augroups with clear=true to avoid duplicate handlers on reload.

rules.rule: Test names describe behavior: it("returns nil when file not found")
Test edge cases: nil, empty tables, boundary values, type mismatches

quick-reference.item: Always local; globals are bugs waiting to happen
1-based; ipairs for sequences, pairs for maps
nil, err return pattern; pcall/xpcall for recovery; error() for preconditions
Return table M; keep implementation local
